correctness.rationale: For all integers \(a,b\ge1,\ell\ge0\) over \(\mathbb C\), the unsigned incidence matrix has rank \(|V|\) because its graph is connected and has an odd cycle, and \(|E|=|V|+1\). The alternating closed-walk vector is primitive, so the edge ideal is exactly one binomial. The two disjoint monomials have parity-determined numbers \((s,t,u,v)\) of unit/squared variables. The Jacobian vanishes exactly on minimal zero supports that are singletons of squared variables or pairs of unit variables, independently on both sides; incomparable coordinate subspaces enumerate the entire reduced singular locus and yield \(N_1,N_2,N_3\). Analytic absorption of nonzero factors gives crossings, \(A_1\) surface nodes and ordinary threefold nodes at general component points. Serre \(S_2+R_1\) gives normal iff \(\ell\le1\). Standalone direct derivative evaluation verified 27,328 binary coordinate patterns for 15 instances; finite checks are not a general proof.

value.rationale: This is a complete parameterized singular-geometry classification for the natural family of two-odd-cycle graph edge hypersurfaces. It quantifies the nonnormal divisorial locus by \(\lfloor\ell^2/4\rfloor\), independently of cycle lengths, and specifies all remaining component counts and transverse analytic germs; these data are motivated by the odd-cycle normality boundary and are useful for studying resolutions and intersection behavior. It is not simply an arbitrary fixed small computation or an unsupported gain: every \(a,b,\ell\) is covered by a symbolic proof.
